$doc: Cases shared by the two strip-ansi implementations: crates/veyyon-shell/src/minimizer/primitives.rs (strip_ansi) and packages/utils/src/strip-ansi.ts (stripAnsi).

One corpus because the two used to disagree, and each disagreement was a real defect rather than a stylistic difference: the Rust half stripped CSI only, so an OSC hyperlink kept its body as visible text in minimized shell output; the TypeScript half read parameter bytes as [0-9;?] rather than the spec's 0x30-0x3f, so a colon-subparameter SGR survived; and the TypeScript half kept a stray escape, which is not a fixed point (see escape_run_settles_in_one_pass).

The contract: remove every well-formed CSI (ESC [, parameter bytes 0x30-0x3f, intermediate bytes 0x20-0x2f, one final byte 0x40-0x7e) and every well-formed OSC (ESC ], a body holding neither BEL nor ESC, terminated by BEL or by ST which is ESC backslash). An escape that opens neither is dropped, alone, and the text after it is kept. Nothing else changes, line endings included.
Both test suites read this file and assert exact equality plus idempotence for every case. Add a case here, not in one language.

cases.name: sgr_color
cases.why: The everyday case: a colored word from any build tool.

cases.name: csi_cursor_and_erase
cases.why: Progress rendering is cursor movement and erase, not color, and it is the bulk of what a captured spinner contains.

cases.name: csi_colon_subparameters
cases.why: A true-color SGR written with colon subparameters, which libvte and several test runners emit. The parameter byte range is 0x30-0x3f, so ':' '<' '=' '>' are parameters too; a class of only [0-9;?] leaves 38:2:255:0:0m behind as visible text.

cases.name: csi_private_mode
cases.why: Hiding and showing the cursor, which every interactive tool does on entry and exit.

cases.name: csi_intermediate_byte
cases.why: A sequence with an intermediate byte (0x20-0x2f) between parameters and the final byte: cursor-shape selection.

cases.name: osc_window_title_bel
cases.why: A window-title set terminated by BEL. Shells and test runners write these constantly, and with no OSC handling the escape was dropped and '0;window title' stayed as visible text.

cases.name: osc_hyperlink_st
cases.why: An OSC 8 hyperlink terminated by ST. Emitted by ls --hyperlink, cargo and clang, so this reaches the minimizer from ordinary builds.

cases.name: osc_body_holds_utf8
cases.why: An OSC body is arbitrary text, including multi-byte characters. Both terminators are ASCII, so a scan that ends on one never lands inside a character.

cases.name: osc_unterminated_is_not_a_sequence
cases.why: A capture cut at a buffer boundary mid-OSC has no terminator. The escape byte goes and the rest is kept as text: deleting to the end of the buffer would lose everything after it, which is the failure the CSI half was fixed for.

cases.name: osc_body_broken_by_an_escape_that_is_not_st
cases.why: An ESC inside an OSC body ends the sequence only as part of ST. Here it opens a real CSI instead, so the OSC never completes and the CSI still goes.

cases.name: csi_truncated_keeps_its_tail
cases.why: The regression the CSI scanner exists for: a truncated escape used to delete the whole tail of the capture.

cases.name: lone_escape_is_dropped
cases.why: A stray escape renders as nothing, so dropping the one byte costs the operator nothing, and it is what makes a pass a fixed point.

cases.name: escape_run_settles_in_one_pass
cases.why: Found by fuzz/fuzz_targets/minimizer_filters.rs. Keeping a stray escape as text let a removal push it against a following '[' and MAKE a sequence, so the same capture minimized to two different things depending on how many passes it had been through.

cases.name: adjacent_sequences_of_both_kinds
cases.why: Sequences arrive back to back, and a scanner that only restarts on text between them misses the second.

cases.name: line_endings_are_preserved_verbatim
cases.why: Stripping decides which bytes are escapes, never how lines end. Carriage returns are a separate primitive's decision and a strip that ate them would hide a \r-overwritten line.

cases.name: text_outside_sequences_keeps_its_characters
cases.why: Multi-byte characters survive intact: the scan copies characters, not bytes.

cases.name: bell_alone_is_not_an_escape_sequence
cases.why: BEL terminates an OSC; on its own it is data. Stripping it would edit output no terminal treats as an escape.

cases.name: plain_text_is_returned_unchanged
cases.why: The fast path. Most captured lines hold no escape at all, and they must come back byte for byte.
